title: [R3-P2-c] Resolve project-stack executable plus entry basenames with win32 semantics on every host
description:
FILED FROM THE THIRD HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #3 (anchored d01c3316, 2026-08-28: 'Request changes - do not merge', 12 P1 merge blockers + P2 follow-ups). Re-verified at HEAD a09b11fa by a read-only verifier; see the ruling memo in the epic channel. Reviewer's finding: R3-P2-c win32 basename + benchmark corpus. Existing rows checked: task-e1b479134f6c4c2282bd7b13af693460(DONE) closesIt=false, task-5ed2d21d26674a669322dfaa0db334be(DONE) closesIt=false, task-24e066557f6747298c9307269d828225(DONE) closesIt=false, task-3a34adcabd03489e84f8dfbec913633a(DONE) closesIt=false, task-c289b8fbcb9840968a9b3994e73b79a4(BLOCKED) closesIt=false. Gap this row closes: (a) is entirely unowned: moe_search_tasks for \"win32 basename\", \"basename\", \"POSIX\", \"node.exe executable basename\", \"Windows path platform-native\", \"project-stack boundary runner\", \"windows-project-stack-boundary\" (incl. archived) returns no row whose DoD touches the boundary's basename decision; the 08-28 review memory maps no row to this P2; no memory or fleet chat message claims the fix; the source file is clean in the shared worktree. It is the single largest contributor to the POSIX root-gate red (15 of 17 root failures on ubuntu and macos at 55dd65ba), so although the reviewer classed it P2 it is on the critical path to \"CI green on all three hosts\". One row drafted below. (b) is a decision wrapped around a gap, and neither half has a row: searches \"benchmark corpus\" (2 hits, both DONE and non-closing), \"pinned document root\", \"MOE_PINNED_DOCUMENT_ROOT\", \"corpus custody untracked documents\", \"pinned benchmark evidence\", \"benchmark skipped CI evidence\", \"maxBuffer porcelain\" find nothing open. The DECISION (human, taskRail 3 and epic rail 1 read-only external artifacts): whether the two pinned documents (benchmark spec Rev 4 sha256 A62B9043...A589C; rebuild design 1D9D1EC9...83191) may be vendored into a tracked location in moe-next or a public corpus repo, given they are untracked in the private corpus, given docs/plans/2026-08-09-benchmark-spec-hash-resolution.md is still AWAITING_HUMAN_RATIFICATION on which revision is authoritative, and given mem:decision-unattested-freeze... records that 0 of 20 benchmark gates are PASS-capable regardless (affiliations/manifest are the real carrier). Until that ruling, a CI corpus cannot be built without either loosening CORPUS_ROOT_DIRTY (forbidden under epic rail 4) or an agent committing documents it does not own. The GAP (agent-fileable once ruled): (i) a cross-host leg that materialises a conforming corpus (tracked documents at a pinned SHA, clean tree) and exports MOE_PINNED_DOCUMENT_ROOT so the 32 arms execute on ubuntu/macos/windows with `0 skipped` in the six suites; (ii) the benchmark gate asserts the skip count (exact expected value or zero) instead of only `Tests N passed`, so a future regression to skip is red rather than invisible. Recommended board action: file a comment on the epic or a governor question naming the custody decision, and hold the CI-corpus row until it is answered; do not file it as if an agent could close it today. Also unowned but adjacent (from the P1.9d handoff): freeze-manifest-admission.ts:99 caps maxBuffer at 64 KiB while this worktree's porcelain is ~870 KB, which can mislabel a large-status corpus as MALFORMED; separate row, not part of this blocker.

Reviewer R3-P2 (anchored d01c3316): packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.ts:103-124 uses platform-native basename for Windows paths instead of win32.basename, causing 15 root-suite failures on POSIX. RE-MEASURED AT HEAD a09b11fa (file clean, untouched since d01c3316): line 1 `import { basename } from "node:path"`; line 112 `basename(nodeExecutable).toLowerCase() !== NODE_BASENAME` refuses PROCESS_BOUNDARY_EXECUTABLE_REJECTED; line 121 `basename(entryPath) !== STACK_ENTRY_BASENAME` refuses PROCESS_BOUNDARY_ARGV_REJECTED. The request contract is Windows-only by construction (isLocalAbsolutePath at windows-path-guard.ts:76-84 refuses any "/"), so on linux/darwin posix.basename returns the whole "C:\\..." string and EVERY curated request is refused at :112 before any other check runs. Real POSIX evidence: cross-host run 33148831675's predecessor 33117388054, job 98675419028 gate (ubuntu-latest) at 55dd65ba: root `Tests 17 failed | 9329 passed | 80 skipped (9426)`, 15 of the 17 FAIL lines are windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts at arms :49, :85, :117, :151-162 (x3), :164-181 (x3), :183-195 (x4), :203, :212; only :100, :131 and :215 pass. macos leg identical. Fix is mechanical: import `win32` from "node:path" and call `win32.basename` at both sites (win32.basename splits on "\\" on every host; "/" is already refused upstream so no widening occurs). Do not add a process.platform branch: the encoder is pure over the request and is unit-tested off-host on purpose (openWindowsProjectStackBoundary keeps its own platform gate at :172).
definitionOfDone: Both basename decisions in windows-project-stack-boundary.ts (HEAD :112 and :121) resolve through `win32.basename` from node:path and the bare native `basename` import is gone. Drill (host-independent, runs on the Windows lane): mutate the fix to `posix.basename` and run `pnpm vitest run packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts`: arms :117, :151-162, :164-181, :183-195, :203, :212 (14) plus :49/:85 go red with EXECUTABLE_REJECTED where ARGV/ENVIRONMENT/MALFORMED or admission was expected; restore, re-run: 18 passed.

The cross-host `gate (ubuntu-latest)` and `gate (macos-latest)` root legs at the fixing commit list ZERO FAIL entries for windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts (baseline job 98675419028 listed 15) and the handoff records both run ids and the root `Tests` count line. Drill: the reverse mutant (native `basename`) on POSIX is already on record as the 15 reds at 55dd65ba; no re-run of the mutant is required, the baseline run id is the control.

All 18 existing arms still pass on windows-latest with no arm deleted, renamed, or loosened, and isLocalAbsolutePath is untouched so a forward-slash executable ("C:/nodejs/node.exe") is still refused. Drill: add or run a probe `encodeProjectStackLaunchPayload({...REQUEST, nodeExecutable: "C:/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe"})` and assert it is not a Uint8Array; a mutant that normalises "/" in the encoder must turn that probe green (i.e. the probe is a real fence).

`pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` exits 0 with the `$ tsc` echo present, and `git diff --stat <parent>..<commit>` names only windows-project-stack-boundary.ts (and its .test.ts if a probe arm was added): no sweep of foreign dirty files from the shared worktree.
taskRails: Owned paths: packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.ts and windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts only. Do NOT touch windows-broker-path.ts (its dirname/join/resolve act on the module's own host location and are correctly host-native) or windows-path-guard.ts.
Never widen the path guard: "/" stays refused, UNC/device namespaces stay refused, no normalisation of separators inside the encoder.
No process.platform branch inside encodeProjectStackLaunchPayload; the request is Windows-shaped by contract and must encode identically on every host so the unit arms remain off-host witnesses.

Evidence must be a POSIX measurement (cross-host run id at the fixing commit), never a Windows-only green: on Windows native basename == win32.basename, so the Windows lane cannot distinguish the fix from the bug.

Commit under this row's id only; the shared worktree carries 400+ dirty foreign files, so stage by exact pathspec and never sweep. Adopt-never-duplicate: if a peer lands win32.basename first, verify and close rather than re-land.
Adopt, never duplicate: re-measure the cited lines at claim time; if a sibling row landed the mechanism first, verify and close rather than re-implement.
